knowledge_point.title: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=2 \\ -4x+24y &=-10.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=2 \\ 0x+0y &=-2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-2$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-2,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}7x+14y &=21 \\ 3x+6y &=9.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}7 & 14 & 21 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}7 & 14 & 21 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=3 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=3-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3-2y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3-2y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & -3 \\ 2 & -10 & -6\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y &=-3 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-5y=-3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=5y-3,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=5y-3 \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5y-3 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).

\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & 6 & -7\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=-6 \\ 0x+0y &=5.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=5$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=5,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

knowledge_point.title: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=6 \\ -4x+8y &=-24.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & -24\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & -24\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=6 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=6.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2y+6,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2y+6 \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2y+6 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+7y &=-2 \\ 6x+42y &=-12.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 6 & 42 & -12\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 6 & 42 & -12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+7y &=-2 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+7y=-2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-7y-2,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-7y-2 \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-7y-2 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
